nim_background_paragraph: I have been invited to participate to the 2025 edition of the Fête de la Science in the University of Strasbourg. I co-animated a computer science stand whose objective was to explain the concept of artificial intelligence (AI) using two workshops of unplugged computing (without computer of screen). Our stand was titled Come defy our cardboard AI !. We presented two workshops showcasing the concepts of artificial learning : the tic-tac-toe game and the game of Nim. This page is dedicated to the game of Nim; the tic-tac-toe game can be consulted on this page.
nim_rules_paragraph_1: The game of Nim is played on a numbered axis with number ranging from 9 to 0. Two players play each other in turn. A single token is placed at the leftmost position on the axis (at the number 9). In each turn, a player must move the token to the right of the axis by a certain number of steps. The only allowed numbers are +1, +2, and +3. The token must move at every turn. The objective of the game is to be the first player to make the token land on the rightmost position on the axis which is the position at the number 1. Warning : in case a move places the token to far right (0 or less), the game will be considered lost !
nim_rules_paragraph_2: The three following animations show different steps in the learning process. The first one allows you to play again a fully-trained AI. This AI has been trained and knows how to win the game. The second one allows you to play against an AI that has not started its learning process yet. It will learn progressively while playing against you and correcting itself. If you play a sufficient number of games against it, it will be identical to the first animation. Finally, the third animation shows you a visualisation of the AI's decision making. It shows the choices the AI makes for every position of the token.
